Brain-derived enrichment reduced ALS confounding of p-tau217

In a multicenter serum study, isolating brain-derived tau increased AD-versus-ALS p-tau217 AUC from 0.729 to 0.900; muscle mass spectrometry detected only big-tau p-tau217, identifying a peripheral source of false-positive signal.

Important new evidence•Peer-reviewed multicenter biomarker and tissue mass-spectrometry study•October 22, 2026

Brain-derived enrichment reduced ALS confounding of p-tau217

In a multicenter serum study, isolating brain-derived tau increased AD-versus-ALS p-tau217 AUC from 0.729 to 0.900; muscle mass spectrometry detected only big-tau p-tau217, identifying a peripheral source of false-positive signal.

Key quantitative results: With direct serum assays, BD-tau and p-tau217 were increased in both AD and ALS versus controls, demonstrating disease-specificity loss from peripheral tau.

BiomarkersBloodp-tau217Brain-derived tauInterference assessment

Added October 24, 2026 · DOI:10.1038/s41467-026-78390-3; PMID:42918778

Evidence summaryDesign, results, and what changed

Thirty-second field brief

The paper moves an ALS p-tau217 confound from observation to mechanism and a possible reflex solution. Standard serum testing was elevated in both AD and ALS. Enriching brain-derived tau removed most ALS signal and materially improved AD-versus-ALS discrimination, while tissue mass spectrometry showed that muscle p-tau217 was exclusively big tau. The method remains experimental.

Study design

Direct serum BD-tau and p-tau217 were measured in 139 people with ALS, 101 with AD, and 75 controls. Brain-derived tau immunoprecipitation was evaluated in a 149-person subgroup (50 ALS, 60 AD, 39 disease controls). Targeted mass spectrometry mapped tau isoforms in brain (n=16), spinal cord (n=11), and muscle (n=10).

Key quantitative results

  • With direct serum assays, BD-tau and p-tau217 were increased in both AD and ALS versus controls, demonstrating disease-specificity loss from peripheral tau.
  • After brain-derived tau enrichment, the p-tau217 signal increased 1.44-fold in AD but fell to 0.42-fold in ALS; ALS and disease controls were no longer distinguishable on the enriched markers.
  • AD-versus-ALS p-tau217 AUC increased from 0.729 to 0.900 (DeLong p<0.001); enriched BD-tau AUC rose from 0.626 to 0.742 (p=0.007).
  • The enriched BD-p-tau217/BD-tau ratio reached AUC 0.961 and exceeded enriched p-tau217 alone (p=0.015).
  • For AD versus disease controls, p-tau217 AUC did not improve significantly (0.941 direct vs 0.919 enriched; p=0.505). Targeted mass spectrometry found exclusively big-tau p-tau217 in muscle.

What changed

The study identifies phosphorylated peripheral big tau in muscle as a mechanism for ALS-associated false-positive p-tau217 and demonstrates a second-line enrichment approach that improves AD-versus-ALS specificity.

Strength of evidence

Moderate-to-strong mechanistic clinical-validity evidence from a multicenter cohort, a within-sample enrichment comparison, and orthogonal tissue mass spectrometry. It remains retrospective; tissue samples were small and unpaired to blood; the enrichment subgroup was 149; and independent assay standardization is absent.

Clinical and field impactInterpretation, implementation, and access

Clinical significance

Unexpectedly high p-tau217 in patients with ALS or major muscle/nerve disease may reflect peripheral big tau. The result supports clinical correlation and cautious confirmatory testing, not routine use of the experimental enrichment procedure.

Field medical relevance

Directly informs assay specificity, comorbidity effects, peripheral interference, reflex testing, treatment-eligibility screening, and the distinction between a commercially measured analyte and its tissue source.

Quanterix or platform relevance

Commercial p-tau217 assays may detect epitopes shared by brain-derived and peripheral big tau. The additional immunoprecipitation step is experimental, pre-analytically complex, and not standardized or routinely available; assay designs with lower big-tau cross-reactivity need direct comparison.

Access or reimbursement relevance

The proposed enrichment step may improve specificity in selected cases but adds specialized laboratory work and is not currently an access, authorization, reimbursement, or coverage pathway.

Likely questionsWhat you may hear and what the evidence supports
Does this invalidate p-tau217 testing?
No. The main issue was distinguishing AD from ALS or peripheral tau signal; AD-versus-disease-control performance was already high and did not improve with enrichment.
Should every positive p-tau217 sample undergo enrichment?
No. The authors frame it as a possible second-line approach for discordant or muscle/nerve-disease cases, and it is not standardized or broadly available.
Is the confound limited to ALS?
ALS was the studied disease model. Other muscle and nerve disorders require direct validation.
Critique and limitationsBias, uncertainty, and missing evidence
  • Retrospective cohorts
  • Enrichment tested in a 149-person subset
  • Small tissue samples not paired to blood
  • ALS was the principal peripheral-disease model
  • Extra laboratory steps and reagent dependence
  • No independent multicenter replication or clinical utility trial
